name: Atmospheric CO₂
summary: CO₂ growth reaches 2 ppm a year as El Niño weakens carbon sinks
state: Mauna Loa recorded 427.2 ppm in the week of 25 Oct, 2.00 ppm higher than a year earlier, reaching the 2 ppm/yr Watch line from 1.59 ppm the previous week. Strong El Niño years usually speed up CO₂ growth as land carbon sinks weaken.
for_you: Faster CO₂ growth means more warming locked in. There is no immediate personal risk; this is a long-run indicator.

sources.title: NOAA GML — Trends in atmospheric CO₂ (Mauna Loa)

why: CO₂ concentration is the main long-run driver of warming; the growth rate shows whether emissions cuts are biting.
drivers: Fossil emissions, land sinks, El Niño (weakens sinks), wildfires.
